findings.issue_text: packages/core/EventManager.ts:118 — `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` is destructured off a possibly-empty array with no optional chaining, so every booking with no destination calendar (the `[]`/`null` sentinel this diff introduces everywhere) throws TypeError before any event is created (conf 100, P0)

packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:73 — Office365 (and Lark:128, CalDAV packages/lib/CalendarService.ts:156) still resolve the target calendar as `destinationCalendar[0]`, ignoring the new `credentialId` arg, so EventManager's per-destination loop calls each host's credential with host #1's externalId: N duplicate/404 writes into the first host's calendar instead of one per host — the collective feature is only implemented for Google (conf 90, P0)

packages/lib/CalendarService.ts:158 — CalDAV/Apple filter `c.externalId === mainHostDestinationCalendar.externalId` yields an empty calendar list for every non-first host's credential, so those hosts silently get zero events and the result is still reported as success (conf 85, P1)

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:256 — `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` is tautologically undefined in the else branch (externalCalendarId is falsy there), destroying the old `destinationCalendar.externalId` fallback; same dead lookup at :317 makes deleteEvent always fall back to `"primary"` and silently fail to delete the real event (conf 100, P1)

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:146 — no destination matching `credentialId` silently degrades to `calendarId: selectedCalendar || "primary"`, so a mis-keyed destination row writes the booking into an arbitrary host's primary calendar with no error surfaced; the list-plus-find design can represent both "two destinations for one credentialId" (first wins, second ignored) and "none matching" as legal states (conf 90, P1)

packages/core/CalendarManager.ts:267 — `externalId` is echoed back from the caller's intent, not from the API response, so when Google falls back to `"primary"` or another calendar the BookingReference records a calendar the event is not in, and every later updateEvent/deleteEvent targets the wrong calendar (conf 85, P1)

packages/core/EventManager.ts:170 — `credentialId: isCalendarType ? result.credentialId : undefined` drops the previous `result.credentialId` fallback for non-calendar (video/conferencing) references, so every video BookingReference is now written with credentialId undefined and can no longer be reconnected to its credential (conf 90, P1)

packages/core/EventManager.ts:381 — the no-credentialId destination branch calls `createEvent(c, event)` with no externalId, so those references get `externalCalendarId: undefined` where the old code used `evt.destinationCalendar?.externalId`, silently regressing update/delete targeting for legacy destinations (conf 80, P2)

packages/core/EventManager.ts:476 — `let calendarReference..., credential;` is declared outside the per-reference loop and only conditionally reassigned, so a failed credential lookup leaves the previous iteration's credential in scope and `result.push(updateEvent(credential, ...))` at :542 updates the wrong host's calendar (or pushes `undefined`) (conf 85, P1)

packages/core/EventManager.ts:342 — per-destination `prisma.credential.findUnique` inside a sequential `for` loop is a textbook N+1 (awaited serially, one round trip per host) where a single `findMany({ id: { in: ids } })` plus a Map keyed by credentialId would be one query; the same hand-rolled credential-hydration block is copy-pasted at :515 and handleCancelBooking.ts:432, with the third copy omitting the `app.slug` include (conf 95, P2)

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:1078 — `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` silently discards every team member's calendar when neither eventType nor organizer has a destination calendar (the array is `null` there), and mutating a just-built literal hides that the collective set is only ever a suffix of the organizer's choice (conf 95, P1)

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:1063 — the ternary is exclusive: when `eventType.destinationCalendar` exists the organizer's own destinationCalendar is dropped while team members' are appended, so the organizer is the one host whose personal calendar never gets the collective event (conf 85, P1)

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:987 — `teamDestinationCalendars` is an unkeyed array with no dedup, so two hosts pointing at the same shared/team calendar (or a member whose destination equals eventType.destinationCalendar) produce duplicate calendar events in the same calendar; the invariant is uniqueness on (credentialId, externalId) and a Set/Map keyed there would enforce it (conf 80, P1)

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:1877 — `connect: { id: evt.destinationCalendar[0].id }` persists only the first destination because Booking.destinationCalendar is still a single FK, so the schema cannot represent the multi-destination state the code now creates and later flows (requestReschedule.handler.ts:240) silently rebuild a one-element array (conf 90, P1)

packages/types/Calendar.d.ts:221 — `createEvent(event, credentialId: number)` makes an internal DB primary key a required positional parameter of the public Calendar interface that every app-store integration must implement, leaking EventManager's credential representation into the plugin contract; the per-credential destination should be resolved before the call and passed as the resolved calendar (conf 80, P2)

apps/web/playwright/webhook.e2e.ts:249 — the webhook payload field `destinationCalendar` is re-typed from object|null to array with no version bump or compatibility shim, so every external consumer reading `destinationCalendar.externalId` breaks, and the new `[]` sentinel is truthy where the old `null` was falsy for any consumer branching on presence (conf 90, P1)

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:1063 — the "none" sentinel is inconsistent across the diff (`null` here vs `[]` in webhook.ts:119, paypal-webhook.ts:152, confirm.handler.ts:175, handleCancelBooking.ts:251), so downstream truthiness checks behave differently depending on which entry point built the CalendarEvent (conf 85, P2)

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:449 — the recurring-deletion block is now nested inside the per-reference loop but does not depend on `reference`, so with R calendar references it re-runs the full credentials x updatedBookings sweep R times: O(R x C x B) duplicate deleteEvent calls to the same events (conf 90, P1)

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:476 — the legacy no-credentialId branch runs every calendar credential for every reference, an O(refs x credentials) fan-out of deleteEvent calls with cross-matched uid/externalCalendarId pairs that mostly 404 (conf 80, P2)

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:689 — `["COLLECTIVE", "ROUND_ROBIN"].includes(eventType.schedulingType)` replaces the `SchedulingType` enum comparison with magic strings (repeated at :992 and :1077), removing the compiler's protection if the enum is renamed or extended (conf 100, P3)

packages/types/Calendar.d.ts:182 — adding `schedulingType` to CalendarEvent stores redundant derived data (nothing in the diff reads it) and forces the shared types package to import the Prisma enum, coupling the calendar contract to the DB schema (conf 75, P3)

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:728 — the loadUsers rewrite drops the `organization: { select: { slug: true } }` selection from the dynamic-user query while users are still consumed as `IsFixedAwareUser` (declared at :354 with a required `organization: { slug: string }`), so dynamic bookings now carry an undefined organization — unrelated scope creep inside a destinationCalendar change (conf 60, P2)

packages/core/EventManager.ts:119 — `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration !== "google_calendar"` dereferences the destructured element without a guard, so any Google Meet booking whose `evt.destinationCalendar` is `[]`/`null` (the very default the diff introduces at handleNewBooking.ts:1067 and every `: []` call site) throws `Cannot read properties of undefined` and the whole booking fails (conf 100, P0).

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:1078 — `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` silently no-ops when neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination calendar (value is `null` per line 1067), so for the headline COLLECTIVE case with no organizer calendar none of the co-hosts' calendars ever receive the event (conf 90, P1).

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:256 — `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` is a tautology that can only ever return the already-known `externalCalendarId`; in the branch where it is used (`externalCalendarId` falsy) it always yields `undefined`, so updates that previously targeted the destination calendar now silently write to the wrong/undefined calendar (conf 90, P1).

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:315 — same tautological `find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` in `deleteEvent`, so cancellations of events stored on a non-primary destination calendar fall back to `"primary"` and leave orphaned events on every host calendar (conf 90, P1).

packages/core/EventManager.ts:170 — `credentialId: isCalendarType ? result.credentialId : undefined` inverts the old `isCalendarType ? evt.destinationCalendar?.credentialId : result.credentialId`, so video (non-calendar) references are now persisted with no credentialId, breaking later meeting update/delete/deleteCredential flows that look references up by credential (conf 85, P1).

packages/core/EventManager.ts:208 — `updateLocation` now writes `externalCalendarId: result.externalId` / `credentialId: result.credentialId` but `updateEvent` in CalendarManager.ts:312-322 returns neither field, so editing a booking location rewrites all calendar references with null externalCalendarId/credentialId and subsequent updates/deletes lose the destination calendar (conf 85, P1).

packages/core/EventManager.ts:542 — `credential` is declared once outside the reference loop (line 479) and never reset, so if the DB lookup for one reference misses, `updateEvent` is called with the previous iteration's credential (updating the wrong host's calendar) or with `undefined` (throwing into the catch and marking every reference failed) (conf 80, P1).

packages/core/EventManager.ts:380 — the no-credentialId destination branch calls `createEvent(c, event)` without passing `destination.externalId`, so the resulting reference has `externalCalendarId: undefined` (line 169) even though the destination calendar is known, regressing the previous `evt.destinationCalendar?.externalId` behaviour and stranding later updates/deletes on "primary" (conf 80, P2).

packages/core/EventManager.ts:554 — the merge-reschedule cleanup still uses `booking.references.find((reference) => reference.type.includes("_calendar"))`, deleting only the first old calendar event; with multiple collective hosts the other hosts' old events are never removed (conf 85, P2).

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:1877 — only `evt.destinationCalendar[0].id` is connected to the booking row, so every downstream consumer that rebuilds a CalendarEvent from `booking.destinationCalendar` (confirm.handler.ts:175, handleCancelBooking.ts:251, webhook.ts:119, bookingReminder.ts:130) sees a single-element array and silently loses the co-hosts' calendars (conf 85, P2).

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:992 — team destination calendars are collected only from `users.slice(1)` for `schedulingType === "COLLECTIVE"`, leaving dynamic group ("collective") bookings — the case the removed TODO at old line 1043 explicitly named — still unhandled, and ROUND_ROBIN/MANAGED untouched with no note of why (conf 75, P2).

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:992 — nothing in the diff adds `destinationCalendar` to any user select (`userSelect.select` spreads at lines 245/320/736/788 are unchanged), so if the shared select omits it the entire feature is a silent no-op; no test or assertion covers that the array ever has more than one element (conf 50, P1).

packages/core/EventManager.ts:339 — no de-duplication of destination calendars: when the event type's destination calendar is also a host's calendar, or two hosts share one, `createAllCalendarEvents` loops per destination and inserts duplicate events on the same calendar (conf 75, P2).

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:427 — the recurring-cancellation branch now sits inside `for (const reference of bookingCalendarReference)` while itself iterating all user credentials × all updated bookings, so with N calendar references each recurring event is deleted N times, producing N-1 spurious failed API deletes appended to `apiDeletes` (conf 75, P2).

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:1067 — this site emits `null` for "no destination calendar" while every other converted site emits `[]`, so consumers must handle three shapes (undefined/null/[]) and the webhook payload shape is inconsistent between BOOKING_CREATED (null, webhook.e2e.ts:119) and BOOKING_REJECTED ([], webhook.e2e.ts:249) with no documented contract for external subscribers (conf 80, P2).

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:750 — the rewritten `loadUsers` dynamic-booking branch drops the `organization: { select: { slug: true } }` selection that the returned users are typed to have (`IsFixedAwareUser`, line 355), an unrelated and unverified removal shipped in this diff (conf 70, P3).

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/organizations/create.handler.ts:151 — `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` was flipped to `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})`, inverting when an organization gets a real slug; this is unrelated to destinationCalendar, untested and unexplained (conf 90, P1).

packages/core/EventManager.ts:336 — zero unit/integration tests accompany a change to the core booking create/update/cancel fan-out; the only verification touched is one Playwright snapshot value (webhook.e2e.ts:249), so none of multi-host creation, per-host reference persistence, or multi-host cancellation is covered by any acceptance check (conf 95, P1).

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:256 — updateEvent's fallback `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` is self-referential and always resolves to undefined when externalCalendarId is null, so legacy BookingReference rows written before externalCalendarId was populated now update against an undefined/primary calendar instead of the destination calendar, silently orphaning the real event (conf 100, P1)

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:315 — same broken fallback in deleteEvent (`externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`) then `calendarId || defaultCalendarId`, so pre-refactor bookings with a null externalCalendarId are deleted from "primary" while the event on the destination calendar is orphaned forever with no way to locate it afterwards (conf 100, P1)

packages/core/EventManager.ts:119 — `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration !== "google_calendar"` dereferences the destructured first element without optional chaining, so every existing/queued CalendarEvent with a null or empty destinationCalendar (handleNewBooking now writes `null`, cron/webhook paths write `[]`) throws TypeError before any booking is created (conf 100, P1)

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:1877 — Booking.destinationCalendar is still a single scalar relation and only `evt.destinationCalendar[0].id` is persisted, so the N team destination calendars used at write time are never recorded; any later read-back path (confirm/cancel/reschedule/payment webhooks) rehydrates a 1-element array and silently stops touching the co-hosts' calendar events (conf 100, P1)

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:1078 — `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` is a no-op when the event type and organizer both lack a destination calendar (evt.destinationCalendar is `null`), so for those COLLECTIVE events every co-host's destination calendar is silently dropped and no event is created for them (conf 100, P2)

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/confirm.handler.ts:175 — opt-in confirmation rebuilds destinationCalendar from the single `booking.destinationCalendar`/`user.destinationCalendar`, so a COLLECTIVE booking confirmed later creates calendar events for only the main host, permanently diverging from the multi-host shape the create path assumed (conf 75, P1)

packages/core/EventManager.ts:169 — BookingReference.externalCalendarId now comes from `result.externalId`, which CalendarManager.createEvent only receives when the destination had a credentialId (the no-credentialId and no-destinationCalendar branches call createEvent without it), so references regress to null externalCalendarId versus the old `evt.destinationCalendar?.externalId` and later update/delete cannot find the event (conf 75, P1)

packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:73 — createEvent ignores the new credentialId argument and always targets `mainHostDestinationCalendar.externalId`, so under a co-host credential the event is written to the wrong (or inaccessible) calendar while EventManager records the co-host's externalId in BookingReference, producing a reference that points at a calendar the event is not in (conf 75, P1)

packages/app-store/larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:128 — same main-host-only calendarId under a per-credential create loop; the co-host credential either writes into the main host's calendar id or throws "no calendar id", leaving partially-created bookings whose references cannot be reconciled (conf 75, P2)

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/organizations/create.handler.ts:150 — slug assignment was inverted from `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` to `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})`, so with billing disabled organizations are now persisted with a null slug and no requestedSlug, creating unroutable org rows that require a manual backfill to recover (conf 75, P1)

packages/core/EventManager.ts:119 — `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration !== "google_calendar"` dereferences the destructured element without optional chaining, so any Google Meet booking by a user with no destinationCalendar (the exact case the fallback exists for) throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'integration')` and the booking fails (conf 95, P0).

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:1078 — `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` is a silent no-op when `evt.destinationCalendar` is null (line 1063-1067 sets null when neither eventType nor organizer has a destination calendar), so the collective multi-host calendars this task adds are dropped exactly when the organizer has no destination calendar (conf 90, P1).

packages/core/EventManager.ts:170 — `credentialId: isCalendarType ? result.credentialId : undefined` replaced the old `: result.credentialId` fallback, so video booking references are now written with `credentialId: undefined`, breaking later video update/delete paths that look the credential up by reference.credentialId (conf 85, P1).

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:256 — `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` only runs the find when externalCalendarId is falsy, so the comparison can never match and `selectedCalendar` is always undefined on that branch, silently sending updates to the wrong/primary calendar (conf 90, P1).

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:317 — same inverted condition in deleteEvent: `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` is only evaluated when externalCalendarId is falsy, so it always yields undefined and deletion falls back to `primary`, leaving orphaned events on secondary/host calendars (conf 90, P1).

packages/core/EventManager.ts:380 — the no-credentialId branch calls `createEvent(c, event)` without the new third `externalId` argument, so `result.externalId` is undefined and the booking reference written at line 169 loses `externalCalendarId` that the old code took from `evt.destinationCalendar.externalId`, breaking subsequent reschedule/cancel targeting (conf 80, P1).

packages/core/EventManager.ts:534 — after the DB fallback, `credential` can still be undefined (credential not found or `app.slug` missing) yet `updateEvent(credential, event, bookingRefUid, calenderExternalId)` is called unconditionally, unlike the guarded `if (credential)` in createAllCalendarEvents, producing a runtime crash inside getCalendar (conf 75, P2).

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:437 — the recurring-booking delete loop is now nested inside the new `for (const reference of bookingCalendarReference)` loop, so with N calendar references every credential/booking deleteEvent is issued N times, multiplying external API calls and pushing duplicate promises into apiDeletes (conf 80, P2).

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:729 — the rewritten `loadUsers` dynamic branch dropped `organization: { select: { slug: true } }` from the prisma select while `IsFixedAwareUser` (line 355) still declares `organization: { slug: string }` and users are force-cast at line 870, so dynamic-group bookings pass users with `organization === undefined` to consumers such as getBookerUrl (conf 60, P2).

packages/core/EventManager.ts:560 — the merge cleanup still uses `booking.references.find((reference) => reference.type.includes("_calendar"))` and deletes only the first old calendar event, leaving stale events on the other collective hosts' calendars now that multiple calendar references exist (conf 70, P2).

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:1078 — `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` silently no-ops when neither eventType nor organizer has a destination calendar (evt.destinationCalendar is `null`), so the stated objective — collecting every collective host's calendar — is skipped exactly in the common team case with no event-type calendar (conf 100, P1)

[]` (same at larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:128 and packages/lib/CalendarService.ts:156) means EventManager's new per-destination loop calls createEvent once per host but every call targets the FIRST host's calendar, producing duplicate events on the main host and none on other hosts — plural type, single-host behavior (conf 75, P1)
